m.title: Modelled explanation
m.q: Explain TWO features of a compiler. [4 marks]
st: Identify the command word, scenario and total marks.
Choose accurate technical terms and examples.
Connect each feature to the consequence in the scenario.
It translates the whole source program before running [1] and produces executable code [1]. Compilation reports translation errors [1] so errors can be corrected before a successful build [1].

w: Explain why an interpreter can be useful during development. [4 marks]

An interpreter executes statements as it processes them [1], allowing tests without producing a separate compiled executable [1]. It can report errors at the statement reached [1], helping programmers locate faults during testing [1].
Compare compilation with interpretation in TWO ways. [4 marks]

A compiler translates the whole program before execution [1], whereas an interpreter translates/executes statements during running [1]. A compiled executable can be run again [1], while an interpreted program normally needs the interpreter to run [1].
